  • companion.node.ble.pin: BLE pairing PIN, this role's own stored override -- see node.ble.pin's help for the general semantics. Reports the stored value, not the resolved active session pin (only meaningful for whichever role is actually live).
  • companion.node.ble.rssi: Current BLE RSSI in dBm -- read-only, same run-time/role-agnostic shape as node.ble.rssi -- companion.node.ble.rssi/repeater.node.ble.rssi both read the same run-time cache regardless of role.

docs.title: board.adc
docs.text:
• board.adc.multiplier: Battery ADC scale multiplier. 0 resets to the board default. Works for both companion and repeater nodes.
  • board.adc.resolution: Battery ADC sample resolution, bits [10|12]. 12-bit is the default, giving ~4x finer quantization than 10-bit at the cost of exposing more raw analog noise. Works for both companion and repeater nodes.

docs.title: board.fem
docs.text:
• board.fem.rssi_offset.lna: dB added to RSSI and the noise floor while the FEM LNA is in the RX path (fem.rxgain on), referring them to the antenna connector. Nominal -17; 0 = no correction.
  • board.fem.rssi_offset.bypass: dB added to RSSI and the noise floor while the FEM LNA is bypassed (fem.rxgain off), referring them to the antenna connector. Nominal +2; 0 = no correction.

docs.title: board.battery
docs.text:
• board.battery.sample_period: Battery resample period [seconds] [1 to 65535], default 300s.
  • board.battery.sample_window: How long before sample_period elapses to start trying for an idle-gated sample [seconds] [1 to 60], default 30s.
  • board.battery.present: Does this node have a real battery installed? {yes|no}. Resolves the ambiguity between 'no battery' and 'battery already full at boot' that voltage alone can't tell apart -- no assumption is made from node type.

docs.title: board.state
docs.text: • board.state.quiet: Bench IR-drop test {on|off}. 'on' sleeps the radio + FEM and suspends mesh/radio work, leaving only the VBAT ADC path live so a bench meter can read board current in isolation. 'off' wakes both live and resumes normal operation immediately -- no reboot needed. Works for both companion and repeater nodes.

docs.title: board.node
docs.text:
• board.node.role: Node role -- ['companion', 'repeater']. Persisted; an actual change always reboots the device. multi_role firmware only.
  • board.node.password: The node's one backup/recovery credential (see beebo config backup/recover) -- distinct from repeater.admin.password (mesh admin login), and present on every build, static companion/repeater included, unlike repeater.admin.password which only exists when the repeater role is compiled in. Unset by default (no compiled-in default, unlike repeater.admin.password's ADMIN_PASSWORD) -- config backup refuses to run until this is set. Write-only, never echoed back on read -- get reports (set)/(unset) only. (write-only, prompts for the value)
  • board.node.id: The ESP32's factory eFuse base MAC (read-only) -- a hardware-burned identifier, stable across reflashes, identity changes, and role switches, unlike companion.node.public_key/repeater.node.public_key (ed25519) or board.node.role (shared).
  • board.node.name: Human-editable alias for board.node.id (DEVICE_NAME plan) -- distinct from the per-role persona names (companion.name/repeater.node.name): this identifies the physical board, not a role. Empty until set; beebo config's default filenames fall back to board.node.id's hex string until then.

docs.title: Console settings (local)
docs.text:
• console.autosave: Whether pref changes are written to flash immediately — {on|off}. On (the default) writes every pref change to flash at once. Off holds changes in RAM only, so they survive until reboot but are not saved — pair it with beebo settings commit to write a batch, or beebo settings restore to roll back.
  • console.transport: Default transport used when no --ble/--tcp/--usb is given — {ble|tcp|usb}. (local to this machine)
  • console.log_level: Default logging verbosity, overridable per-run with --log-level. (local to this machine)
  • console.dbg_level: Default minimum debug-event severity monitor debug/monitor watch stream, when no H/M/L is given in their own KINDS arguments — H | M | L. (local to this machine)
  • console.device_id: Optional: a human-readable record of which board.node.id this alias is meant to point at. Not auto-verified against the live device on connect (see common/config.py's module docstring for why). (local to this machine)
  • console.device_name: Optional: this alias's device.name label, purely informational. (local to this machine)
  • console.node_name: Auto-learned on this alias's first successful connect: the live device's board.node.name. Every later connect verifies the live device still matches, refusing on a mismatch (see common/config.py's module docstring). Clear it (empty string) to re-learn after an intentional device swap under this alias. (local to this machine)
  • console.node_role: Auto-learned alongside node_name (see there) -- the live device's role (companion|repeater) at that connect. Same verify-on-connect/clear-to-re-learn behavior as node_name. (local to this machine)

docs.title: console.ble
docs.text: • console.ble.address: Default BLE MAC/name; 'scan' discovers and picks a device. (local to this machine)

docs.title: console.tcp
docs.text: • console.tcp.host: Default TCP host[:port]. (local to this machine)

docs.title: console.usb
docs.text: • console.usb.port: Default USB serial port path. (local to this machine)

docs.title: repeater.routing
docs.text:
• repeater.routing.rxdelay: Base delay before relaying [s] [0 to 20], independent of companion.routing.rxdelay. Staggers repeats so neighbors that all heard a packet don't collide.
  • repeater.routing.airtime: Transmit budget [#] [0 to 9], independent of companion.routing.airtime. Scales the enforced wait between this node's own transmissions; 0 is unthrottled, higher values ease congestion.
  • repeater.routing.seen_window: How long [seconds, fractional] [0 to 60] a repeat of a packet still counts as the same packet: a duplicate, or the echo of our own send that arrived after its echo window (credited as heard, so the confirm ratio and the trial scores do not charge a late echo as a failure; beebo analyze dup-latency sizes it). It also decides whether a dedup-table eviction counts as a live risk (beebo monitor status's rx_dedup_table_full row). Independent of companion.routing.seen_window. Stored as milliseconds. 0 turns the late credit and the live-eviction counting off (a real, literal setting, not a 'reset to default' sentinel); firmware default is 30.
  • repeater.routing.retry: Coding rates 4/x of the retries of a forwarded flood whose echo timed out, in order, up to three [5 to 8 each]: 5|6 retries first at 4/5 then at 4/6. 5 is the same rate as the first send, 8 the most robust (longest airtime). 0 disables retries.
  • repeater.routing.dutycycle: Repeater's own airtime budget as a channel-occupancy percent [%] [1 to 100], independent of companion.routing.dutycycle. A friendlier view of repeater.routing.airtime; writes airtime_factor = 100/percent - 1.
  • repeater.routing.txdelay: Base TX delay factor [0 to 2], scales the random wait before this node's own transmissions.
  • repeater.routing.direct.txdelay: TX delay factor for direct (non-flood) transmissions [0 to 2].
  • repeater.routing.agc.reset.interval: AGC reset interval [s], rounded to a multiple of 4.
  • repeater.routing.interference.threshold: Interference threshold [0 to 9]. Higher values require a noisier channel before the radio reports interference. (CommonCLI wire key stays "int.thresh" -- only this path's name changed, per SETTINGS_TREE_CLEANUP.md Decision D.)
  • repeater.routing.tuning.adaptive.enabled: Adaptive tuner on/off — {on|off}. Observe-only by default: logs MON_ADAPTIVE proposals to the monitor ring every 5 min. Whether a given param's proposals actually get written live is controlled separately by tuning.adaptive.applied. Independent of the trial (tuning.trial.enabled). RAM-only — always back to 'off' after a reboot.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.adaptive.applied: Per-param live-actuation bitmask [0 to 63], bit i = AdaptiveController::specFor(i)'s param (0=rx_delay_base, 1=tx_delay_factor, 2=direct_tx_delay_factor, 3=agc_reset_interval, 4=interference_threshold, 5=airtime_factor). A clear bit keeps that param observe-only; 0 (default) means every param stays observe-only. RAM-only — always back to 0 after a reboot.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.adaptive.window.min_s: Shortest evaluation window, seconds [1 to 65535, <= max_s]; default 300. RAM-only. Invalidates the window in progress.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.adaptive.window.max_s: Longest evaluation window, seconds [1 to 65535, >= min_s]; default 3600. A window with no RX activity at max_s is insufficient_data. RAM-only. Invalidates the window in progress.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.score.routed: Weight of packets routed per hour (confirmable attempts; a retry is not one) in the score both tuners judge windows with [-50 to 50], in tenths (10 = 1.0, 0 = ignored, negative = a cost). Defaults: routed 10, delivered 10, received 0, which is the confirmed deliveries per hour. RAM-only. Refused while a trial is running; between trials it restarts the trial sequence and the adaptive tuner's statistics.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.score.delivered: Weight of the share of the routed packets that were confirmed in the score both tuners judge windows with [-50 to 50], in tenths (10 = 1.0, 0 = ignored, negative = a cost). Defaults: routed 10, delivered 10, received 0, which is the confirmed deliveries per hour. RAM-only. Refused while a trial is running; between trials it restarts the trial sequence and the adaptive tuner's statistics.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.score.received: Weight of valid packets received per hour in the score both tuners judge windows with [-50 to 50], in tenths (10 = 1.0, 0 = ignored, negative = a cost). Defaults: routed 10, delivered 10, received 0, which is the confirmed deliveries per hour. RAM-only. Refused while a trial is running; between trials it restarts the trial sequence and the adaptive tuner's statistics.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.enabled: On-device A/B trial master switch — {on|off}. A trial runs only when this and that switch's switches.<lna|rxboost|cr>.enable are on. Independent of the adaptive tuner (tuning.adaptive.enabled). RAM-only — always back to 'off' after a reboot. Turning it off aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.rxboost.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of RX boosted gain in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.rxboost.values: Values of RX boosted gain the trial explores [0 to 1]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,1). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.lna.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of FEM LNA in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.lna.values: Values of FEM LNA the trial explores [0 to 1]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,1). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.agc.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of AGC reset interval [s] in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.agc.values: Values of AGC reset interval [s] the trial explores [0 to 1020]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,8,16,32). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.interference.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of interference threshold in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.interference.values: Values of interference threshold the trial explores [0 to 9]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,3,6,9). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.cad.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of CAD in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.cad.values: Values of CAD the trial explores [0 to 1]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,1). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.cr.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of coding rate in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.cr.values: Values of coding rate the trial explores [5 to 8]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 5,6,7,8). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.multiacks.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of multi acks in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.multiacks.values: Values of multi acks the trial explores [0 to 1]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,1). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.retry.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of retry policy in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.retry.values: Values of retry policy the trial explores (policies separated by commas, each 0 or 1 to 3 coding rates from 5 to 8 separated by '|'): A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,5,5|6,5|7). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.rxdelay.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of RX delay base in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.rxdelay.values: Values of RX delay base the trial explores [0 to 20]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,7,13,20). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.txdelay.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of TX delay factor in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.txdelay.values: Values of TX delay factor the trial explores [0 to 2]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,0.5,1,2). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.directtxdelay.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of direct TX delay factor in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.directtxdelay.values: Values of direct TX delay factor the trial explores [0 to 2]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0,0.5,1,2). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.airtime.enable: Include the on-device A/B trial of airtime factor in the sequence [0 to 1]; 1 = yes (default: all are on, so tuning.trial.enabled runs the whole sequence). One switch runs at a time when tuning.trial.enabled is on, in the order rxboost, lna, agc, interference, cad, cr, multiacks, retry, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime; a switch turns itself off once decided. A trial changes it live only (a reboot reverts it) and persists the winner. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.airtime.values: Values of airtime factor the trial explores [0 to 9]: A first, then 1 to 3 challengers, separated by commas (default 0.5,1,3,9). The sequence first stores A; the first trial compares A with the first challenger, each later one compares the winner, which is persisted, with the next challenger. A challenger equal to the winner is skipped. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.confidence_pct: Trial confidence level, percent [90, 95 or 99]; default 95. How sure the node must be before it adopts the alternative: 100 minus it is about the most often a trial of a setting with no real gain adopts it, counting every look (sequential t-test on the paired score difference); higher adopts less readily and needs more pairs. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.min_gain_pct: Smallest worthwhile score gain, percent [0 to 50]; default 5. When even the best case of the trial's confidence interval is below it, the trial stops early and keeps the original. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.min_pkt_rate: The score's own events per minute (confirmed deliveries for the default score; normalized so a uniform scale of the score weights does not change it) a FIXED schedule (block_size_s and block_count both set) needs before its next trial starts, and that every A B B A cycle of a running one must clearly average [0 to 255]; default 5, 0 = no minimum and no idle stop. A planned (auto) schedule adapts to any rate and ignores it. Below it before a start the sequence waits, checking once a minute; below it over a cycle the trial ends idle, keeps the original and runs again an hour later, and three in a row turn tuning.trial.enabled off. RAM-only. A running trial keeps the value it started with for its idle stop.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.profile: Which switches a trial sequence runs and how many values each tries — {main|exhaustive}. main (default): the FEM LNA, CAD, TX delay factor and retry policy, one challenger each against the stored value. exhaustive: every switch with its full value list. Selecting a profile sets the switches' .enable and resets their .values. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.start: Where a trial sequence starts — {stored|list}. stored (default): each switch's A is its stored value, the last winner, and every list value is a challenger. list: the sequence first stores each switch's first list value as A. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.combined: Run one combined trial instead of one per switch — {on|off}. Side A has every participant at its stored value, side B at its current challenger (the first list value with start stored, the second with start list); a switch participates when selected and its B differs from its A, and at least two must. A win adopts every participant's B. Every selected switch is done after it. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.block_size_s: Trial block length, seconds [0 = auto, 1 to 3600]; default 0: set before every A/B/B/A cycle from the node's traffic so a block holds about 50 of the score's events. Blocks alternate A/B/B/A so each hour of day is compared like for like. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.block_count: Most blocks per trial [0 = auto, 2 to 1000], rounded down to whole A/B pairs; default 0: planned from the confidence, min gain and the noise the trial measures, or the trial is skipped as underpowered; it ends earlier when the decision bounds settle it. With block_size_s also set the schedule is fixed. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.tuning.trial.block_spread_pct: Advanced: override of the block spread a trial's first plan starts from, percent [0 to 70]; default 0 = built-in (14: c = 0.02), the relative standard deviation of a block that a longer block does not average away. Higher starts with more pairs. A running trial moves it toward what its own pairs show, so it rarely needs setting. RAM-only. Aborts a running trial.
  • repeater.routing.loop.detect: Flood-loop suppression aggressiveness — {off|minimal|moderate|strict}.
  • repeater.routing.flood.max: Max hop count for flood-routed packets [0 to 64].
  • repeater.routing.flood.max_advert: Max hop count for flood-routed adverts [0 to 64].
  • repeater.routing.flood.max_unscoped: Max hop count for unscoped flood packets [0 to 64].

docs.title: repeater.guest
docs.text: • repeater.guest.password: Guest/room-server login password (not the repeater's own admin password — see repeater.admin.password). Read back in cleartext over a legacy CommonLink text connection; write-only over a binary (multi_role) connection, same as repeater.admin.password — treat beebo settings repeater.guest.password as a secret-revealing command when it does read back. (write-only, prompts for the value)

docs.title: repeater.fem
docs.text:
• repeater.fem.rxgain: Front-end module RX gain / LNA — {on|off}. Switches the FEM's low-noise amplifier into the receive path for better weak-signal sensitivity, at a little extra receive current. Distinct from the SX1262's own boosted gain (radio.rxgain); only present on boards whose FEM supports it. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.fem.rxgain/repeater.fem.rxgain.
  • repeater.fem.txgain: Front-end module TX gain / PA — {on|off}. Software-selectable external FEM transmit gain; not a PA power switch. Only present on boards whose FEM supports it. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.fem.txgain/repeater.fem.txgain.

docs.title: repeater.radio
docs.text:
• repeater.radio.lora.freq: Carrier frequency [MHz] [137 to 1020]. Must sit in a band legal for your region and match the nodes you talk to directly.
  • repeater.radio.lora.bw: Channel bandwidth [kHz] [7.8, 10.4, 15.6, 20.8, 31.25, 41.7, 62.5, 125, 250, 500]. Wider is faster but less sensitive; must match the nodes you talk to directly.
  • repeater.radio.lora.sf: Spreading factor [#] [5 to 12]. Higher reaches further but is slower; must match the nodes you talk to directly.
  • repeater.radio.lora.cr: Coding rate denominator [#] [5 to 8] (4/N). More redundancy survives noise but costs throughput.
  • repeater.radio.lora.preset: Named community-suggested freq/bw/sf/cr quadruplet for a region (from presets.json, mirroring meshcore.nz's own app config) — reading reports the matching preset title or '(custom)' if the live quadruplet doesn't match any of them; writing applies all four fields from the named preset at once, e.g. 'beebo settings companion.radio.lora.preset "USA/Canada"'.
  • repeater.radio.txpower: Output power at the PA [dBm] [-9 to board max].
  • repeater.radio.rxgain: SX1262 RX boosted-gain mode for weak-signal reception — {on|off}. Independent of the FEM/LNA (fem.rxgain). This role's own independent copy -- see companion.radio.rxgain/repeater.radio.rxgain.
  • repeater.radio.cad: Hardware channel activity detection before each transmit — {on|off}. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.radio.cad/repeater.radio.cad.

docs.title: repeater.monitor
docs.text:
• repeater.monitor.enabled: Global capture switch — {on|off}. Pause/resume the ring by toggling this.
  • repeater.monitor.rx: Capture RX records — {on|off}.
  • repeater.monitor.tx: Capture TX records — {on|off}.
  • repeater.monitor.radio: Capture RADIO reference records (config changes) — {on|off}.
  • repeater.monitor.env: Capture ENV reference records (noise/battery/heap) — {on|off}.
  • repeater.monitor.batt: Capture BATT records (every Vbat sample, idle/forced + trend state) — {on|off}.
  • repeater.monitor.tuning: Capture tuning records — {on|off}: the adaptive tuner's proposals (tuner), the evaluation windows (eval) and the A/B trials (trial).
  • repeater.monitor.path: RX path mode — {on|off}: an RX record's nbr holds the last three hops of its path, one byte each (the first byte of each hash), instead of the last hop's identity. Off by default. With 2- and 3-byte hashes two neighbors can share a byte.
  • repeater.monitor.event: Capture EVENT records (fault transitions and other notable state changes, timestamped instead of a bare sticky flag) — {on|off}. On by default. Same bit as setting/command/route/debug below (see their own help) -- toggling any of the five toggles all five.
  • repeater.monitor.setting: Capture SETTING records (admin-visible setting changes) — {on|off}. Alias of event -- same bit, no independent toggle (see its help).
  • repeater.monitor.command: Capture COMMAND records (admin commands run) — {on|off}. Alias of event -- same bit, no independent toggle (see its help).
  • repeater.monitor.route: Capture ROUTE records (periodic routing-latency snapshot) — {on|off}. Alias of event -- same bit, no independent toggle (see its help).
  • repeater.monitor.debug: Capture DEBUG records (folded-in RLOG transport/boot/session trace) — {on|off}. Alias of event -- same bit, no independent toggle (see its help).

docs.title: repeater.profile
docs.text: • repeater.profile.enabled: Enable/disable ProfileLog (command/span latency profiling ring, see beebo profile) — {on|off}. Off by default; inactive until turned on explicitly. Distinct from monitor.* (MonRing's own capture config) -- ProfileLog measures span duration, a separate concern. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.profile.enabled/repeater.profile.enabled.

docs.title: repeater.admin
docs.text: • repeater.admin.password: Admin/owner login password used for mesh login/cmd auth (distinct from guest.password). Defaults to the firmware's own compiled-in ADMIN_PASSWORD until changed (varies by build env -- not always the literal "password"). The value itself is write-only, never echoed back on read (over a binary connection, get instead reports (default)/(set): a server-side comparison against ADMIN_PASSWORD via GET_PREFS_TLV(KEY_REPEATER_PASSWORD), mirroring node.wifi.password's (set)/(unset); unavailable at all over a CommonLink, no CommonCLI text-CLI equivalent exists). Run beebo settings repeater.admin.password with no value and you'll be prompted for it hidden, twice — a plaintext CLI argument is rejected outright since it'd already be in your shell history before any confirmation could help. Even a successful set only proves what's in RAM/ComPrefs, not that the mesh login check accepts it — verify with beebo admin <target> login <newpwd>. (write-only, prompts for the value)

docs.title: repeater.node
docs.text:
• repeater.node.name: The repeater persona's own advertised name (distinct from companion.name) -- stored at /com_prefs offset 4. Empty until customized, in which case the device falls back to the companion name.
  • repeater.node.repeat: Whether this node forwards other nodes' traffic — {on|off}. Off turns the repeater into a leaf node (advertises but doesn't relay).
  • repeater.node.multi_acks: Whether this node sends multiple ACKs for multi-path replies [#], independent of companion.multi_acks (companion's own copy, companion_settings.py).
  • repeater.node.path_hash_mode: Path hash length used for new contacts [0=1 byte, 1=2 bytes, 2=3 bytes], independent of companion.path_hash_mode (companion's own copy, companion_settings.py).
  • repeater.node.adv_loc_policy: The repeater persona's own advertised-location policy [0=none, 1=share, 2=prefs], independent of companion.adv_loc_policy (companion's own copy, companion_settings.py). 'share' reads the shared, role-agnostic live-GPS register, which stays 0,0 on beebo (no GPS hardware) -- deliberately not seeded from repeater.coords, so an accidental 'share' is obviously wrong rather than silently acting like 'prefs'. Use 'prefs' (backed by repeater.coords) for a fixed location.
  • repeater.node.coords: The repeater persona's own advertised coordinates [deg], as 'LAT,LON', independent of companion.coords (companion's own copy, companion_settings.py).
  • repeater.node.allow.read.only: Whether unauthenticated clients may read (but not change) prefs over the console — {on|off}.
  • repeater.node.advert.interval: Interval between local (zero-hop) adverts [minutes], 60 to 240, or 0 to disable.
  • repeater.node.advert.flood_interval: Interval between flood adverts [hours], 3 to 168, or 0 to disable.
  • repeater.node.owner.info: Free-text owner/contact info shown to guest logins.
  • repeater.node.region.home: This repeater's home region -- a bookmark only (RegionMap's own home_id). No forwarding or send code anywhere reads it; it exists purely for 'region tree'/'region home' to show which region you consider yours. See repeater.node.region.default for the region that actually tags this node's own outgoing traffic -- home_id and default_id are two genuinely independent RegionMap fields (same as stock simple_repeater keeps them), not synced with each other. 'none'/'0'/empty clears this bookmark (binary connection only -- no CommonLink equivalent for clearing, only reading/setting). Setting this to a region name that doesn't exist yet auto-defines it first (root-level, flood-allowed by default -- same as a bare beebo region put <name>), so this always applies directly.
  • repeater.node.region.default: The region this repeater's own outgoing traffic (self-adverts, flood replies) is actually tagged with -- RegionMap's own independent default_id/getDefaultRegion(), GET/SET_REGION_DEFAULT (distinct from repeater.node.region.home's home_id). Restores stock simple_repeater's own default-scope mechanism, which multi_role's repeater role didn't consult until this was wired up -- it used to fall back to companion.node.region.scope (companion's own field, companion_settings.py) as a stand-in, which this leaf is now unrelated to. Setting this to a region name that doesn't exist yet auto-defines it first (root-level, flood-allowed by default), matching CommonCLI's real 'region default <name>' behavior exactly.
  • repeater.node.region.list: Read-only inventory of this repeater's defined region names. Over a CommonLink this is only the flood-allowed subset (CommonCLI's text-CLI has no unconditional 'list everything' form); over a binary connection it's every defined region regardless of its flood-allow/deny flag.
  • repeater.node.public_key: Repeater's own Ed25519 public key (read-only) -- distinct from companion.node.public_key (companion_settings.py) and from node.public_key (whichever role is currently live).
  • repeater.node.tz_offset: Hours from UTC [-12 to +14], stored for the app's CLI (get/set tz.offset); nothing on the node uses it. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.node.tz_offset/repeater.node.tz_offset.
  • repeater.node.transmit: Whether the radio sends anything — {on|off}. Off is receive-only: no forwards, adverts, ACKs or replies, and beebo cw is refused; stricter than node.repeat, which only stops relaying. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.node.transmit/repeater.node.transmit.
  • repeater.node.transport.ble: Whether this role brings up BLE at boot — {on|off}. This role's own independent copy -- see node.transport.* for the general semantics (live-apply behavior, ble/tcp mutual exclusion, usb fallback).
  • repeater.node.transport.tcp: Whether this role brings up TCP at boot — {on|off}. This role's own independent copy -- see node.transport.* for the general semantics (live-apply behavior, ble/tcp mutual exclusion, usb fallback).
  • repeater.node.transport.usb: Whether this role brings up USB at boot — {on|off}. This role's own independent copy -- see node.transport.* for the general semantics (live-apply behavior, ble/tcp mutual exclusion, usb fallback).
  • repeater.node.wifi.ssid: WiFi network name (SSID) the node joins to offer the TCP companion transport. This role's own independent copy -- see companion.node.wifi.ssid/repeater.node.wifi.ssid.
  • repeater.node.wifi.password: WiFi password, write-only (see node.wifi.password's help for why). This role's own independent copy. (write-only, prompts for the value)
  • repeater.node.wifi.ip: Current WiFi station IP address, assigned at run time by DHCP once the node joins its configured network -- read-only. Not really a per-role value (there's one physical WiFi radio, whichever role is live) -- companion.node.wifi.ip/repeater.node.wifi.ip both read the same run-time cache regardless of role. Empty means WiFi is off or the node hasn't associated yet.
  • repeater.node.wifi.rssi: Current WiFi STA RSSI in dBm -- read-only, same run-time/role-agnostic shape as node.wifi.ip. No BLE equivalent: BLE RSSI can't be read synchronously on this hardware without racing a live BLE teardown (see fw's SerialBLEInterface::requestHealthSample() comment), so it isn't exposed at all. WIFI_RSSI_UNAVAILABLE (127) means WiFi is off or the node hasn't associated yet.
  • repeater.node.ble.pin: BLE pairing PIN, this role's own stored override -- see node.ble.pin's help for the general semantics. Reports the stored value, not the resolved active session pin (only meaningful for whichever role is actually live).
  • repeater.node.ble.rssi: Current BLE RSSI in dBm -- read-only, same run-time/role-agnostic shape as node.ble.rssi -- companion.node.ble.rssi/repeater.node.ble.rssi both read the same run-time cache regardless of role.

docs.title: Support and Feature Requests
docs.text: Beebo is a one-person project, built and supported in spare time. Questions, bug reports and ideas are welcome, and I read them all. Replies can take a while, so thank you for your patience. This is a hobby project, and a clear, friendly report gets the fastest answer.

docs.title: Where to ask
docs.text:
Bug reports and feature requests go through the issue tracker of the firmware repository: github.com/pasqo/beebo-meshcore-fw/issues

You need a free GitHub account. Search the open and closed issues first: your question may already be answered. Then choose New issue, pick the bug report or the feature request form, and write one issue per problem or idea.

For questions and open discussion, the MeshCore Discord firmware-development channel is a good place too.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
The bug report form asks for what helps me reproduce it:

  • what you did, what you expected and what happened
  • the firmware version (ver on the node console, or beebo status node) and the board
  • the role the node was in, companion or repeater, and how you connect (app, USB, BLE or WiFi)
  • the output of the commands involved, copied as text (status, check, monitor status)
  • for a crash or a reboot loop, what the node printed over USB

Never post secrets: admin passwords, private keys, WiFi passwords or the files of config backup.

docs.title: Asking for a feature
docs.text: Say what you want to do, not only the feature you have in mind, and why the current behavior falls short. A real use case helps decide what to build.

docs.title: Before you ask
docs.text: Troubleshooting covers the common messages, and Commands lists what runs on the node and on the computer. For MeshCore itself (apps, packet formats, the mesh) see the MeshCore documentation.

docs.title: What to expect
docs.text: Fixes and features happen when I have time, in an order that suits the project. Some requests may wait, or be declined to keep beebo small and reliable. A thank-you note, or a star on the repository, is always appreciated.

docs.title: Trial Reference
docs.text: Everything about how a setting trial works and how to read its result: the profiles and switches, the sequence, the statistics, the schedule, and the beebo analyze commands.

docs.title: Profiles and switches
docs.text:
Some settings are high-impact and depend on the local environment, so the adaptive tuner does not tune them. A separate on-device trial decides them instead: it compares two values of one setting on the live node and keeps the better one. Twelve settings can be trialed, one after another, in the order of the table below.

Which of them run is the trial profile, repeater.routing.tuning.trial.profile:

  • main (default): the LNA, CAD, TX delay factor and retry policy, each against one challenger (the last column). The other eight rows also have a one-challenger list in this profile, used if you enable them by hand.
  • exhaustive: all twelve settings with the full lists of the third column.

Selecting a profile sets the switches' .enable bits and resets their .values to the profile's lists. Like the other trial settings it is RAM-only, so a reboot returns it to main. The feed and trial records print the two compared values in the setting's internal units: on/off switches as 0/1, the delay factors in hundredths (txdelay a=50 b=100 is 0.5 against 1.0), rxdelay in tenths, agc in units of 4 s, and retry as a policy byte (64 is one retry at 4/5).

Switch Setting Default .values (A first) main: selected, B lna fem.rxgain 0,1 yes, on rxboost radio.rxgain 0,1 no, on agc routing.agc.reset.interval (seconds) 0,8,16,32 no, 8 interference routing.interference.threshold 0,3,6,9 no, 3 cad radio.cad 0,1 yes, on cr radio.lora.cr 5,6,7,8 no, 6 multiacks node.multi_acks 0,1 no, on retry routing.retry 0,5,5\|6,5\|7 (a policy is its coding rates separated by \|) yes, 5 rxdelay routing.rxdelay 0,7,13,20 no, 5 txdelay routing.txdelay 0,0.5,1,2 yes, 1.0 directtxdelay routing.direct.txdelay 0,0.5,1,2 no, 0.5 airtime routing.airtime 0.5,1,3,9 no, 1.0

Each switch has a group repeater.routing.tuning.trial.switches.<name> (listed in run order by beebo settings) with two leaves:

  • .enable (0/1, default 1): the switch is part of the sequence. A switch turns itself off once it is decided.
  • .values: the values it explores, A first and then up to 3 challengers separated by commas, for example 5,6,8. The defaults start at the upstream setting and span the allowed range (the airtime default leaves out 0, which removes the duty-cycle limit). A list of n values is n - 1 trials.

docs.title: How a sequence runs
docs.text:
1. Turn repeater.routing.tuning.trial.enabled on (independent of the adaptive tuner). The profile decides the switches: four with main (the default), all twelve with exhaustive; set .enable to 0 on the ones to leave out. A switch that is off is never touched. Turning the trial on also sets the monitor to record it, persisted: it enables the monitor and the tuning, event and radio capture and the trial_pkt_rate event, and turns rx and tx capture off so that a long run does not fill the ring (turn them on afterwards with beebo monitor capture rx on).
  2. Where the sequence starts is tuning.trial.start. With stored (the default) each switch's A is its stored value, the winner of the last run, and every value in its list is a challenger (one equal to A is skipped), so runs build on each other. With list the node first sets every selected switch to the first value of its list and stores it, so the run starts from a known state whatever was stored before. The default lists start the LNA off and RX boost on (the Heltec V4 default), so the radio still hears traffic while the LNA is measured.
  3. A planned trial starts as soon as the node has traffic data. With tuning.trial.block_size_s and tuning.trial.block_count at their default 0 (auto) the node plans the schedule (see Automatic schedule below) and holds the sequence only until it has counted events of each indicator the score weights. A planned schedule adapts to whatever rate there is: it has no rate floor, runs at any rate, capped at 72 hours, and ends idle only when a whole cycle counts nothing. With both set the schedule is fixed, and then a trial starts only while the node counts at least tuning.trial.min_pkt_rate events a minute (default 5; 0 = no minimum, and no idle stop either). The events are the score's own, those whose chance variation sets a block's noise: the confirmed deliveries for the default score, the routed attempts for a routed-only score, the received packets for a received-only one (a mix of weights gives the equivalent of the weighted sum; the rate is normalized by the largest weight squared, so scaling every score weight by the same factor does not change it). monitor tuning trial shows the rate as counting N/min. Below the minimum the sequence waits, checking once a minute, and logs a trial_pkt_rate event each time it starts or stops waiting. The same rate ends a running fixed trial (step 5), when a cycle counts clearly less than the minimum: more than 3 standard deviations under it, since counts vary by about their square root.
  4. The first switch runs. Its first trial compares A with the first challenger: every block (tuning.trial.block_size_s seconds) the value alternates in an A/B/B/A pattern, for tuning.trial.block_count blocks (two per pair). Half the blocks run the other value, so expect reduced service during the trial. A fixed schedule that spans every hour of the day, 30 minute blocks for 96 blocks, compares like for like.
  5. After every pair from the third on, the node checks whether the evidence has settled, on the paired difference of the score (see How noisy a trial is). It keeps A as soon as even the best case for B is smaller than a worthwhile gain (tuning.trial.min_gain_pct, default 5%). It adopts B as soon as even the worst case is a real gain with no loss in confirm ratio (more than 2 percentage points), unless B's confirmed deliveries grew: more forwarding lowers the ratio without losing anything. The bounds are the mean of the paired change plus or minus t x sqrt(N / n) standard errors, with n the pairs so far, N the most pairs the trial may run and t the Student-t value at the confidence level tuning.trial.confidence_pct (90, 95 or 99 percent, default 95); the factor sqrt(N / n) is what lets the node look after every pair, so the bounds are wider than the plain interval until the last pair. A clear result ends the trial early. confidence_pct is how sure the node wants to be before it changes a setting: 100 minus it is about the most often a trial of a setting with no real gain adopts B, counting every look, not each look alone (the rule is the plain t value scaled by sqrt(N / n), close to the nominal rate but not exact). Each switch's trial has its own budget, so over a sequence of switches the expected number of false adoptions adds up. B is adopted when the lower bound is above 0, not above min_gain_pct: min_gain_pct sets the pairs the plan asks for and the point below which A is kept. monitor tuning trial shows the bounds and Conf, the confidence they amount to: 100 minus it is the p-value adjusted for the looks, and B is adopted when it reaches confidence_pct. It is not the probability that B is better. An undecided trial whose bounds stopped moving ends as inconclusive with A kept (it needs at least 7 pairs); otherwise it runs to the end of the schedule, where B is adopted only if the plain test passes; otherwise, or with fewer than 3 pairs, it ends undecided with A kept. Before that test, after every pair, the node checks for a dead side: a block that heard nothing never forms a pair, so a setting that deafens the radio would otherwise lose by default. When one value heard at most a quarter of the other's packets (Received, counted up to 8 per block), the other heard traffic in at least 2 blocks, and a split that uneven is too unlikely to be chance, the value that hears wins at once. After every A/B/B/A cycle of a fixed schedule, an average clearly below tuning.trial.min_pkt_rate events a minute over the whole cycle (a planned schedule: no events at all) ends the trial as idle with A kept: the channel is too quiet to decide anything. The switch stays pending and the same trial runs again an hour later; a run of idle ends with no completed trial for 24 h turns tuning.trial.enabled off.
  6. The winner is stored before the next trial starts. The next trial compares that winner with the next challenger of the list, and a challenger equal to the winner is skipped.
  7. When a switch has run out of challengers the node turns its .enable off and moves to the next switch. When every selected switch is decided it turns tuning.trial.enabled off too; turn them on again to run another sequence.

docs.title: Combined trial
docs.text:
A one-switch trial resolves a gain only when it is large: a 1-2% switch never does at 10 packets a minute, and its trend is thrown away. Several such gains add up and resolve together. So screen the switches one by one for a trend (the Change and Conf columns of monitor tuning trial), then set tuning.trial.combined on and run one trial where side A and side B differ in all of them at once.

  • Side A is each selected switch's stored value. Side B is its current challenger: with tuning.trial.start stored the first value of its values list that differs from the stored one, with list the second value. Put the direction its screening trend favored first, or set values to A,B.
  • A switch takes part when it is selected, its B differs from its A, and it can run (the FEM LNA needs LNA control). Anything else changes nothing. Fewer than two participants ends as skipped (same).
  • The decision is the usual paired test. A win adopts every participant's B; there is no per-switch attribution. Every selected switch is decided afterward, whatever the outcome (an idle end retries the whole combination an hour later).
  • A manual change of any participant aborts the trial, as for one switch.
  • monitor tuning trial shows a combined row (A and B are the two sets) and marks the participants in combined; analyze tuning trial lists the participants.

docs.title: What changes and what is kept
docs.text:
• The four radio switches (lna, rxboost, cr, cad) act on the radio hardware live only: a reboot in the middle of a trial puts the stored value back. The other eight settings are read by the node from its running settings, so a trial writes its value there while it runs and puts the original back afterwards.
  • Only a winner is stored, and the sequence stores A at its start. So the stored settings of the selected switches change when a sequence starts, and stay changed if you stop it. Every change is logged as a setting record with source tuning.
  • A packet pool guardrail trip ends the running trial with A kept (outcome aborted_guardrail); the sequence goes on with the switch's next challenger, or the next switch. Disabling the trial or changing any tuning.trial.* setting aborts the running trial and restores the setting. Changing a tuning.trial.* setting restarts the sequence for the switches still selected: it stores their A again, so it undoes a winner adopted for a switch that has not finished (a finished switch is off and is not touched).
  • A manual change of a switch's own setting during its trial (through beebo settings or the binary protocol) aborts that trial; the switch's trial then starts again with the new stored value as A.
  • Caveat: for the six settings held in the running settings (agc, interference, rxdelay, txdelay, directtxdelay, airtime), any other setting change while their trial runs also saves the challenger value, and a set typed in the repeater's text CLI for the same setting is overwritten by the trial.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
All RAM-only and back to their defaults after a reboot: tuning.trial.enabled (off), .profile (main), .switches.<name>.enable and .values (above), .block_size_s (0 = auto, or 1 to 3600 s), .block_count (0 = auto, or 2 to 1000), .block_spread_pct (0 = built-in start, advanced, 0 to 70), .confidence_pct (95), .min_gain_pct (5), .min_pkt_rate (5 events a minute, the start gate and the idle stop of a fixed schedule; see steps 3 and 5) and .start (stored, or list; see step 2).

Each block is logged as MON_EVAL, and the trial itself as MON_TRIAL records: a start (setting and sides), one per block (the sequential rule's mean and bounds so far) and an end (outcome and statistics), see beebo monitor decode -k trial. They are captured only with repeater.monitor.tuning on.

docs.title: How noisy a trial is
docs.text:
A trial decides from the paired differences d of the score between an A block and the next B block, so what limits it is how much d varies when the setting makes no difference. Two things add to that:

  • Counting noise, v: a block holds a limited number of events, and the score moves by chance with their count. v = 1/N, where N is the counts per block of the score: for the default score, which is the confirmed deliveries per hour, the confirmed deliveries in the block (the routed attempts for a routed-only score, the received packets for a received-only one), so a block with 33 of them has v of about 0.03 (a 17% swing). A longer block averages it down.
  • The block spread, c: bursts of traffic, slow drift over the day, and an effect that differs from pair to pair. The same in a long block as in a short one, so longer blocks do not average it away.

A block's variance is v + c, a pair difference has twice that, and with P pairs the trial can tell a gain g (gain, 5% by default) from nothing at the confidence t (about 2 at 95%) when P is about 2 t² (v + c) / g². With v = c = 0.03 that is about 190 pairs. Once a block holds about 1/c confirmed deliveries, more length buys little; more pairs do. The ratio phi = var(d) / (2 v) says how far a trial is above counting noise alone: 1 is counting noise only, and it grows with block length.

beebo analyze tuning phi measures these on pulled trials (see Analyzing trials). On 13 trials pulled from one repeater (300 s and 900 s blocks) the block spread is 14% (c = 0.020, 0.007 to 0.039), about 51 counts per block (N), and phi is 1.2 to 1.3 for 300 s blocks and 2.5 to 3.1 for 900 s blocks.

docs.title: Automatic schedule
docs.text: With block_size_s or block_count at 0 the node plans the missing one from its own traffic, so the confidence and min_gain_pct you asked for are reachable. A background tracker keeps the routed, confirmed and received rates of the last few hours (an average that fades with a two hour time constant), ready once it has seen 5 confirmed deliveries over 30 seconds, so a node that just booted can plan within minutes. From those rates and the score weights the plan takes the block length that holds about 50 counts of the score (the confirmed deliveries for the default score; 60 s to 1 h), the most pairs from the formula under How noisy a trial is, and the block spread c that starts at the built-in 0.02 (a 14% swing, what the field trials pooled to). That start is only a first guess and needs no setting (block_spread_pct, 0 = built-in, overrides it as an advanced setting): once a running trial has 4 pairs, each re-plan moves the spread toward what the pairs show, c = var(d) / 2 - v (the variance of a block less its counting noise, measured around the mean difference, so it does not depend on the effect under test), weighted as the pairs seen against 3 pairs for the start. A noisier channel than the start lengthens the trial, a quieter one shortens it, so the most pairs move up or down as the trial learns. A planned trial has no rate floor (min_pkt_rate applies to fixed schedules only): it runs at whatever rate there is, with longer blocks when the rate falls. A schedule that needs more than 72 hours or 1000 blocks is underpowered: the trial runs capped at those limits and ends when a decision bound is crossed or the cap is reached, inconclusive if the data does not decide. With only one of the two set the other is planned; a fixed block_count is never checked for feasibility and never re-planned. The settings keep reading 0: the planned values are in the trial's start record and plan records. monitor tuning trial shows, next to each auto setting, the schedule of the trial running now (auto (running trial: up to 304 blocks), auto (running trial: 150 s now, set per cycle)) or what the node would plan for the next one (auto (next trial: ...)), or that it is still collecting traffic data, has no counts for the score yet, or the plan is underpowered. Under them, at most 152 pairs, 8h31m left at the current traffic is what the trial can take at the traffic it sees now, with the remaining blocks as long as they are now (they follow the traffic). It ends earlier when a decision bound is crossed. The table's N column is the counts per block that set its noise, 1/N: the confirmed deliveries for the default score, the routed attempts for a routed-only score, the received packets for a received-only one (a mix gives the weighted sum's equivalent). Bounds is the node's decision interval at the pairs so far and Conf the confidence it amounts to (100 minus Conf is the p-value adjusted for the looks), the figure to compare with confidence_pct: B is adopted when Conf reaches it.

docs.title: How slow a node can be
docs.text:
The block length follows the rate, 3000 / rate seconds for 50 events, and the pairs needed do not, so the time a trial can take scales with 1 / rate. The longest trial at the built-in block spread (c = 0.02), in hours, by events a minute (the figures are computed from the planner's formulas, not measured on a node):

events a minute 95% confidence, 5% gain 90%, 5% gain 90%, 10% gain 20 12 8 2 5 44 32 9 3 73 (capped) 53 15 2 109 (capped) 79 (capped) 22 1 217 (capped) 157 (capped) 44

The pairs are 130, 94 and 26 (260, 188 and 52 blocks). A longest trial above 72 hours runs capped at 72 hours. A trial usually ends earlier, at about 60% of the longest in simulation, when a decision bound is crossed. So with the defaults the practical limit is about 3.5 events a minute; a larger min_gain_pct or a lower confidence_pct lowers it. Below it the trial runs capped at 72 hours and is likely to end inconclusive. Blocks stop growing at 1 h (below about 0.8 events a minute), the noise then rises, and a trial that spans hours of changing traffic measures a larger block spread than the start value, which the plan follows after a few pairs.

block_count auto is the most blocks the trial may run, not a fixed schedule: the trial ends as soon as the decision bounds settle it, and the pairs it needs depend only on the confidence, min_gain_pct and the noise. block_size_s auto is the block length now. After every A B B A cycle the node plans again from the rates of its last four A blocks (side B changes the rates, side A does not carry the effect under test, so the plan never sees the result). The next cycle's four blocks take the length that holds about 50 counts at that rate, all four alike so every pair stays comparable and drift still cancels inside the cycle, and a change of less than 15% is ignored so a noisy rate does not move it every cycle. The noise of a block stays about the same whatever the traffic does, so the pairs needed stay about the same and the time changes: a quiet hour gives longer blocks, a busy one shorter ones. With block_count auto the pairs also grow or shrink to the noise measured, up to the 72 hour cap, counted from the start of the trial; a block at its 1 h ceiling cannot hold the counts, so the noise rises and the pairs grow. A trial whose schedule hits the cap runs to it and decides there. A planned trial waits 10 s after each switch of the value before it starts counting a block (the confirmations of packets sent before the switch are not counted), and ends early as inconclusive once even the full schedule could not decide. Shorten a trial by raising min_gain_pct, or lowering confidence_pct, or fixing block_count. analyze tuning trial prints the plan, each re-plan (with the block length it set), where the decision stands and the noise the blocks measured.

docs.title: The trial report
docs.text:
beebo analyze tuning trial prints this report; its options are under Analyzing trials.

The report of one trial starts with a header, then the plan, the noise, the decision and the table of indicators:

A finished trial of radio.cad on a repeater: B was clearly worse, so the node kept A after 7 of up to 64 pairs

Received per side is what the dead-side check counts; its split p appears once one value hears at least four times the other.

Status says whether the trial ended (and how: at which pair and why, or that the schedule completed), is running, or was interrupted (no end record and the capture runs on without another block). Ended and Verdict appear once the node has written the end record. The table has one row per indicator with the mean of A and B over the matched pairs, Change (the per-pair B - A, mean and standard error), Conf (two-sided Student t confidence that the change is not zero) and a Verdict. The columns match monitor tuning trial: Pairs, N and Bounds are the score's and show - on an indicator row.

The first row, Score, is what the trial optimizes and decides on: the objective's log score, whose A and B are the score as a packet rate per minute (confirmed deliveries for the default weights, so B / A - 1 is the Change) and whose Change is shown as a relative gain in percent (e^x - 1 of the log-score difference, so it reads against min_gain_pct), with the trial's verdict (use A, use B, inconclusive, use A, undecided, use A, use B (A heard almost nothing) or the reverse, or an abort reason); before 3 pairs it reads undecided, and without an end record so far: ... shows what the node's own rule gives. The rows Routed, Delivered and Received are the score's indicators; the rows below them are diagnostics (TX Dispatched, RX Invalid, RX Errors, Nbr Heard, Nbr Marginal, Pool Busy, CAD Busy). Where higher is better they show B better or A better once their confidence reaches the trial's confidence setting, and B ahead or A ahead below it; the rest show -. The trial re-derives the decision offline with the node's own rule and flags a difference from the node's end record. Blocks the node marked insufficient_data or invalidated are excluded from the pairing.

docs.title: beebo analyze tuning trial — reading a setting trial
docs.text:
beebo analyze tuning trial [FILE] reports the latest setting trial in one pulled day file (the most recent by default; a relative FILE is resolved against --dir). A trial record is captured only with repeater.monitor.tuning on. For a trial with a planned schedule it also prints the plan (block length, blocks and pairs, block spread, the traffic it planned from, pairs run) and the noise the node measured (var(d)/2, counting noise v, phi). A set can also be named before the report, like every other analyze report (gatto analyze monring_2026-09-27 tuning trial), but it must be a raw .bin set. When the newest set holds no trial, the report says which set does.

$ gatto monitor pull
$ gatto analyze tuning trial
Option Effect --all Detail every trial in the file, not just the latest --blocks Add the per-block table (every indicator, one row per block) --legend Print the definition of every column and verdict word first --score NAME=WEIGHT,... Re-score the blocks offline with these score weights (tenths, -50 to 50; routed, delivered, received; one not named is 0), e.g. --score received=10. The node's own verdict is unchanged and shown in a note --diagnostics Also chart the diagnostic indicators; by default only Score, Routed, Delivered and Received are charted (the table lists all rows) --json JSON instead of tables

With more than one trial in the file (a sequence), a "Trial Plan" table comes first: one line per trial with its setting, A, B, start, status (ended, running or interrupted), the pairs used of those planned, N (the counts per block that set its noise, 1/N), Spread (the block spread, see how noisy a trial is) and verdict, with the pool over the trials under it. The report also has a Decision line: the bounds at the pairs measured of the most the trial may run, the widening by the planned pairs, the two thresholds, and the confidence against the one needed. Every trial report has a Noise line from its measured blocks: N, φ with its 95% interval, the block spread with c and its interval against the planner's built-in start of 14%, and the pairs this noise needs to resolve the minimum gain; --json carries it as phi. The trial report explains each column.

docs.title: beebo analyze tuning phi — how noisy the trials are
docs.text:
The per-trial figures are part of analyze tuning trial; this command pools them over every trial of a set.

beebo analyze tuning phi [FILE] measures how noisy the paired score differences of every finished trial in a pulled set are (the most recent by default; --from NAME, a leading dataset name or --all for every raw set under --dir). A block's variance is v + c: v the counting noise (1/N, N the counts per block of the score: the confirmed deliveries for the default score), c the block spread, the part that longer blocks do not average away (bursts, drift, an effect that differs between pairs). φ = var(d) / (2 v) is 1 for counting noise alone and grows with block length. See How noisy a trial is.

$ gatto monitor pull
$ gatto analyze tuning phi --all

It prints one row per trial with at least 3 measured pairs (setting, start, block length in seconds, pairs, confirm ratio p, counts per block N, mean paired difference, φ), the pool per setting and block length, and the overall pools with 95% intervals: φ, and the block spread (the standard deviation sqrt(c) in percent, with c and its interval) and the block size N = 1/c (counts per block) beyond which longer blocks add little, ending with whether a reference block spread of 14% (c = 0.02) is inside c's interval. The reference is the planner's built-in start; the command's constant is not a device setting. Trials it cannot use are listed with the reason (too few pairs, or a received weight on a capture without the on-device rx counter). --score NAME=WEIGHT,... re-scores with other weights as in analyze tuning trial; --json prints the same as one object.

beebo analyze tuning effect splits the whole capture by setting assignment (lna, rxgain, tx_power, any changed setting; -p picks which) and reports the indicators for each, plus the change against the longest-running assignment computed hour by hour so time-of-day load cancels.

docs.title: Setting Trials
docs.text: A repeater can test its own settings on live traffic. For one setting it runs the current value (A) and one alternative (B) in alternating blocks, scores each with the packets it handled, and keeps the better one. Each setting is tested alone, so a result can be traced to a single change.

docs.title: Run one
docs.text:
On a repeater, from the CLI screen or the beebo-cli channel:

settings routing.tuning.trial.enabled on
> on

That is all. monitor tuning trial shows where it stands. To run only some of the switches, name them: monitor tuning trial start lna cad (or all). Turning a trial on also sets what it needs on the node:

  • It enables the monitor and the capture kinds a trial writes (tuning, events, radio changes), and turns packet capture off so that a long run does not fill the ring.
  • If the transmit power is under 16 dBm it posts a warning. Trial results at a power that underdrives the amplifier are not worth much. Fix it with settings radio.txpower 18.
  • If the node hears too little traffic it posts trial waiting for traffic and starts by itself when traffic arrives.

Stop at any time with monitor tuning trial stop. A reboot stops a trial as well, because the trial settings are not saved. A winner that was already decided stays.

docs.title: What gets tested
docs.text:
The default profile, main, tests four settings, each against one alternative:

Setting A (current) B Why it is in LNA (fem.rxgain) as stored on Sensitivity against tolerance to interference: site dependent. CAD (radio.cad) as stored on Channel-activity detection before sending. TX delay (routing.txdelay) as stored 1.0 Spread of retransmissions, to avoid collisions. Retry (routing.retry) as stored one retry at coding rate 4/5 Whether a retry rescues forwards that got no echo.

A setting whose alternative already equals the stored value is skipped. The exhaustive profile tests all twelve settings with their full lists, which takes much longer:

settings routing.tuning.trial.profile exhaustive
> exhaustive

A profile change is lost at a reboot, which returns the node to main. The twelve switches and their values are listed in the Trial Reference.

docs.title: How long it takes
docs.text:
The node sizes each trial to the traffic it counts, so a busy node decides quickly and a quiet one takes a day or more per setting. The start line says what to expect:

beebo-mr: trial cad start profile=main a=0 b=1 blocks=260 block=493s

Here: 260 blocks of 493 seconds, 36 hours at most for that setting, fewer if the evidence settles earlier.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Result Meaning keep_a B was no better. The current value stays. adopt_b B was clearly better. The node switched to it, and keeps it across reboots. inconclusive, undecided Not enough evidence. The current value stays. skipped_same B equals the current value, so there was nothing to compare. skipped_no_control The node cannot control that setting (for example the LNA on a board without LNA control), so there was nothing to compare. skipped_underpowered The traffic is too low for the schedule to decide inside the 72 hour cap. The trial is skipped instead of running to inconclusive. alive_a, alive_b One side heard almost nothing against the other. The side that hears wins at once (see the dead-side check in the Trial Reference). aborted_changed The setting was changed by hand, or the trial was disabled, while it ran. The setting is restored. aborted_guardrail The packet pool guardrail tripped. A is kept and the sequence goes on. aborted_idle The channel was too quiet to decide. A is kept, the switch stays pending and runs again an hour later.

The result line carries the score gain of B over A and its standard error. To read the records (per-block scores, confidence, noise), pull them and analyze them from the command line:

$ beebo monitor pull
$ beebo analyze tuning trial

The options, the report columns and the statistics are in the Trial Reference.

docs.title: Companion role
docs.text: Trials run in repeater role only. A companion answers ERR: needs role 'repeater', node is 'companion'.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
For how connections behave and why, see Connections.

What you see Why What to do The app or CLI gets no answer from the node Only one connection drives the node at a time. Another app, the beebo CLI or a USB session may hold it. Disconnect the other client. settings board.node.role repeater gets no reply A role switch reboots the node by design. Wait a few seconds and reconnect. ERR: needs role 'repeater', node is 'companion' The node is a companion. Switch the role first: settings board.node.role repeater. trial waiting for traffic The node hears too little traffic to start a trial. Wait. It starts by itself when traffic arrives. warn: txpower=<n> dBm underdrives the PA The transmit power is under 16 dBm. settings radio.txpower 18 Unknown command The node does not know that command. Check the spelling. Commands lists what the node answers and what needs the beebo command line. ERR: unknown setting The path is not one the node console knows. settings lists the names, and settings <branch> the ones below it. The rest of the tree needs beebo settings. ERR: the trial is already on; run monitor tuning trial stop first A trial is running. Stop it, then start again. ERR: battery.present is no; set it to yes first battery state <state> cannot force a state on a node without a battery. settings board.battery.present yes. The trial stopped after a reboot Trial settings are not saved across a reboot. Enable it again. The app cannot connect after flashing beebo A pairing made with firmware that used an older BLE stack does not carry over. Remove the node from the phone's Bluetooth list and pair again with PIN 123456. The two beebo channels are missing The app has not synced yet, or the node's channel table is full. Reconnect. With a full table no feed is created. A new board does not boot beebo A board that never ran MeshCore needs a stock image first. Flash a stock MeshCore companion in merged mode with the Web Flasher, once, then the beebo image. An update failed The node rolls back to the previous image if the new one does not boot. Check the version, then try again. The node's clock is wrong, for example years ahead The clock only moves forward, so a normal sync cannot correct a clock that is ahead. beebo clock shows the drift. beebo clock --boot reboots the node with the host's time.

Still stuck? See Support and Feature Requests.

docs.title: Performance Tuning
docs.text:
A repeater's delivery performance is governed by a handful of runtime parameters that shape how it reacts to what it hears: how long it waits before repeating a flood packet, how it jitters retransmissions to avoid colliding with other nodes, how aggressively it defers to channel activity, and how much of its own airtime budget it spends. The right values are not a one-time bench setting. They depend on local traffic density, RF conditions and mesh topology, which drift over time and differ per deployment.

Beebo measures this on the node itself and can decide the settings for you.

To... Read Let the node test its own settings and keep what works Setting Trials Look up a profile, a switch, a statistic or a schedule Trial Reference Understand what each parameter controls in MeshCore How a Repeater Routes See how a result is scored Scoring Read the loop-time, headroom and latency metrics Monitoring Use the older, experimental live optimizer The Adaptive Tuner

To run a trial see Setting Trials. The full repeater.routing.tuning.* leaf list is in Settings.

docs.title: Update and Service a Node
docs.text: Updating firmware and servicing a deployed node from the beebo command line. All beebo firmware changes are backward compatible with existing MeshCore companion applications.

docs.title: Over-The-Air (OTA) FW Update
docs.text:
Once a beebo firmware is resident in the node, you can update the firmware remotely without physical access in around 30 seconds. For example, to flash a firmware image when connected through any of the available transports, run beebo ota with the path of the .bin file:

An OTA update over WiFi: the image is streamed to flash in 22 seconds and the node reboots into it

The CLI shows dual progress bars: Transfer tracks bytes sent to the device, Flashing tracks bytes written to the OTA partition. Chunk and buffer sizes are printed before the transfer starts.

The device validates the new image on first boot and rolls back automatically if it fails to start.

Flash speed varies by transport. The firmware file is split into chunks and each chunk is sent through a synchronous round trip (send → flash write → OK), so the bottleneck is the number of round trips times the per-chunk SPI flash overhead.

  • WiFi uses 8 KB chunks (about 215 round trips for 1.7 MB) and typically completes in under a minute. This is the recommended transport for OTA updates.
  • USB also uses 8 KB chunks.
  • BLE uses 174-byte chunks (about 10,000 round trips) and is the slowest due to additional inter-write spacing.

Note that the only benefit of using USB OTA (which really is not over-the-air but rather Over-The-Cable) over regular USB flashing with esptool is that it does not require manually putting the board in program mode as is the case for the Heltec V4.3 and maintains the RTC clock, apart from a skew of few seconds.

docs.title: Verify Firmware Version
docs.text:
After flashing or OTA, verify the running firmware version. For instance using WiFi on the beebo node:

$ beebo status node
              Node
╭───────────┬──────────────────────╮
│ Name      │ Beebo                │
│ Role      │ companion            │
│ Model     │ Heltec V4.3 Headless │
│ Version   │ 1.18.0.beebo.1.0     │
│ Build     │ 15-Jul-2026          │
│ Transport │ TCP - myssid         │
│ WiFi RSSI │ -45 dBm ▂▄▆█         │
╰───────────┴──────────────────────╯

docs.title: OTA Transfer and Priority Mode
docs.text:
Incoming OTA chunks are written straight to flash via esp_ota_write, which batches partial sectors internally — no app-level PSRAM buffering. It uses the standard ESP-IDF dual-partition scheme: the new image is written to the inactive OTA partition while the current firmware keeps running, then esp_ota_set_boot_partition switches over on reboot.

beebo ota has a --priority flag, on by default and honored on every transport (BLE, USB and WiFi): the node skips normal radio and mesh dispatch for the duration of the upload, so the OTA stream is not delayed by loop work, trading mesh responsiveness for upload speed. Live mesh traffic can slow an upload several times over without it. Use --no-priority to keep servicing the radio during the transfer.

docs.title: Admin Transport Control
docs.text:
The beebo admin <target> transport [usb|ble|tcp [on|off]] subcommand reads or toggles a node's transports remotely over the mesh admin channel, and beebo admin <target> transport (or get transports) queries all three at once — useful for flipping WiFi on for OTA on a deployed repeater and back off afterward without physical access. Admin requests retry automatically on the underlying request/response exchange.

This enables servicing repeater nodes very effectively through TCP, by switching TCP on only when needed, servicing, and turning it off leaving the repeater a lower power idling state. For instance, the workflow to update the gatto repeater node FW quickly through the beebo companion node, while both nodes are within WiFi reach (perhaps a mobile AP if in the nodes are in the sticks):

# Turn on tcp on gatto through the mesh.
# We omit -t beebo because it is our default transport and node.
$ beebo admin gatto transport tcp on
OK - tcp is now ON

# Update gatto to the release image
$ beebo -t gatto ota heltec-v4-1.18.0.beebo.1.0.bin
OTA upload: heltec-v4-1.18.0.beebo.1.0.bin (1768016 bytes)
  1.17.1.beebo.1.0 (Build: 14-Jul-2026)  →  1.18.0.beebo.1.0
Finalizing ... ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 100% 52.6 kB/s 0:00:00
OTA completed in 33s — rebooting into 1.18.0.beebo.1.0.

# Turn off TCP on gatto to restore average idle current of 50mA instead of
# idle current pf 125mA with TCP/BLE radio on.
$ beebo -t gatto settings repeater.node.transport.tcp off

# Or alternatively through the mesh:
$ beebo admin gatto transport tcp off
OK - tcp is now OFF

Note that to toggle transports on and off, one can also use the MeshCore Phone and Desktop application admin cmd <target> "<cmd>", where commands are get {usb|ble|tcp} or set {usb|ble|tcp} {on/off}.
